name: Sidebar nav
purpose: The persistent vertical navigation of a desktop application frame: a full-height column of grouped destinations with exactly one current location, which collapses to an icon-only RAIL without losing its accessible names. Use it where the product is an application the user stays inside, rather than a site they pass through. Itinerary row 36 (P2, 'Desktop app frame nav').
$status: PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed — new component, built through the gated-component route at #203 wave 3b lane I. Nothing about it is ruled, least of all whether it should exist separately from Navigations.

props.name: collapsed
props.$note: false = 248px expanded column; true = 64px rail. The toggle carries aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: groups
props.$note: Ordered groups. A group may be a plain labelled list or a COLLAPSIBLE section with its own disclosure button.

props.name: currentHref
props.$note: Drives aria-current="page" on exactly one link. More than one current location is a defect, not a variant.

props.name: footerItems
props.$note: Persistent utilities pinned below the scrolling body — settings, help, sign out.

props.name: count
props.$note: Optional per-row count chip (.nv-count). 24px on a row, 18px in the rail. Rounded — Badge and Avatar are the ruled exceptions to square corners, and a count is a Badge wearing a nav row.

props.name: disabled
props.$note: Renders aria-disabled=true + tabindex=-1. The row keeps its place in the reading order rather than vanishing.

props.name: user
props.$note: The bottom account slot: avatar initials, name, role, chevron. Hidden to a name-only tooltip in the rail.

props.name: lockup
props.$note: The top product slot: masterbrand SVG (#230) plus a product word. Type set to look like a logo is the defect that ruling exists to stop.

variants.name: expanded
variants.use: the default desktop column: icon + label, group headings visible

variants.name: rail
variants.use: collapsed to 64px, icon-only, labels visually hidden but present in the accessibility tree

variants.name: overlay
variants.use: Under 768px the same column slides in over a scrim from a menu button. Escape or the scrim closes it and focus returns to the button. One class (.is-narrow on the frame), no forked markup.

tokens.rule: divider/border/section — the outer frame and the column's right edge
tokens.sub-rule: divider/border/subsection — between groups and around the header and footer
tokens.hover: tertiary/background/hover — hover AND the current row's ground
tokens.indicator: primary/border/default (#DB0011, both modes) — the 3px current-location bar
tokens.radius: border-radius/surface (0; Console renders 20 via s199-D3, which is Dave's ruling arriving correctly)
tokens.$note: The indicator follows the one gated navigation artefact: Navigations.reference.html:27 marks its current masthead item with an inset box-shadow in the same brand red. Copied, not invented.

mustNotNeighbour: A second primary navigation on the same screen — one primary nav per screen

behaviour.fallback: Every row is a native `<a>` and stays focusable and in the tab order; the authored `aria-current="page"` stands and both its visual carriers (the 3px leading bar and the surface change) follow it, because they are bound to the attribute in CSS. What goes: clicking another row never moves `aria-current`, Space does not activate, the arrow/Home/End focus walk is gone, the collapsible group cannot be toggled (it renders in the `aria-expanded`/`hidden` state the markup authors), and the rail collapse toggle does nothing.

$note.current: "You are here" is a STATE, not an authored fact — the measured defect was a static aria-current no interaction could move. Each `nav.sn` is its own scope, so two specimens do not share a current location.
$note.keyboard: NO roving tabindex by decision: a nav list is not a composite widget, so arrows move FOCUS only and every destination stays in the tab order. Hidden rows (a collapsed group) are skipped.
$note.group: Collapsible group is Accordion's disclosure, ARIA first: aria-expanded on the button, `hidden` on the list it names through aria-controls; the chevron rotation is CSS on [aria-expanded="true"].
$note.rail: Rail collapse copies App-shell-side-nav's mechanics scoped to the column: labels are hidden, never removed, so accessible names survive; the toggle swaps its label, the chevron href and the nav's own aria-label.
$note.$unproven: Prose derived from the snippet's own script and comments at #258 L3, not from a driven probe.

accessibility.landmarks: A <nav> landmark with an accessible name. The rail keeps its own name so the two states are distinguishable in a landmark list.
accessibility.currentLocation: aria-current="page" on exactly one link — 'page' because the destination IS a different page (Anchor nav uses aria-current="true" for the same reason inverted).
accessibility.collapse: The toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the body it collapses.
accessibility.collapsibleGroup: A group heading that opens a sub-list is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, not a link.
accessibility.railNames: Labels are visually hidden (clip-path), never removed, so every rail item keeps a text-derived accessible name and no aria-label restates it. #261 CLOSES THE #203 OPEN FINDING: in the rail the SAME hidden label is re-shown in place as a tooltip on :hover and :focus-visible, so the sighted mouse user and the screen-reader user are told the same word. Tooltip is not composed in; nothing was invented.
accessibility.targetArea: Every link is min-height 44px; the rail item is 64x44; the collapse toggle is 44x44.
accessibility.colourIndependence: Current location is carried by aria-current + a bar whose presence/absence is a shape difference + a surface change. Colour is third, never alone.
accessibility.disabledRows: A disabled destination is aria-disabled=true + tabindex=-1, not a removed row. Pointer events are off, the arrow-key walk skips it, and its count chip drops its fill for a 1px outline so no contrast claim is made on a surface WCAG exempts. (#261)
accessibility.overlay: The overlay is a DISCLOSURE, not a dialog: no role=dialog, no aria-modal, no focus trap — the column is still the same <nav> landmark and claiming otherwise would lie to AT. What it owes the keyboard is the return trip: Escape or the scrim closes and focus goes back to the menu button. (#261)

antiPatterns: Marking the current item with the red bar ONLY — it measures 2.73:1 in Supercharge dark and is a problem hue for an astigmatic reader either way
Dropping labels from the accessibility tree when the rail collapses (aria-label restating a label that already exists is the milder version of the same mistake)
A rail with no tooltip — a mouse user gets an unlabelled icon column and no way to learn what it means
Two links carrying aria-current at once
Using this AND a masthead primary nav on the same screen
Animating the collapse without honouring prefers-reduced-motion

tokenValidation.$finding: THE CURRENT-LOCATION BAR IS UNDER THE 3:1 FLOOR IN SUPERCHARGE DARK. primary/border/default (#DB0011) on the ground it sits beside — on tertiary/background/hover, which is what a current row renders: mono 4.58 light / 3.01 dark · legacy 4.58 / 3.01 · console 4.58 / 3.01 · SUPERCHARGE 3.89 light / 2.73 dark FAIL. On the resting raised surface: 5.22/3.16 in three themes, 4.84/2.88 FAIL in Supercharge dark. It is deliberately NOT declared as a contrastPair — that would be a green that cannot fail in the one theme where it is false (#174 precedent). The component leans on the SHAPE carrier and aria-current instead. PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed: Supercharge dark either needs its own current-location value, or the pattern needs a non-red mark in that theme.
tokenValidation.$collision: CHECKED FIRST-HAND, NOT ASSUMED (#203 step 0). Navigations.reference.html is 64 lines and renders one <header> — a horizontal web masthead. Its meta CLAIMS a family (anchors, nav-bar-bottom, nav-bar-top) the artefact does not contain, and its own $finding admits 'a web masthead only'. Nothing in that family is a persistent vertical column and nothing in it collapses. PROPOSED #203, Dave's: Sidebar nav stands alone, or is absorbed as a `type` of Navigations. Component promotion is on the DO-NOT-RULE list, so it is surfaced and left open.

responsive.$note: #261 ANSWERS THE #203 DEFERRAL. It read: 'Below the desktop breakpoint the correct answer is almost certainly a Drawer, not a rail. NOT specified here.' Specified now, PROPOSED not ruled: below 768px the column becomes an OVERLAY over a scrim, opened from a menu button in a compact top bar. It is the same markup and the same class grammar — only .is-narrow on the frame and data-open on the column change. The rail stays the DESKTOP density control, not the mobile answer.

$navFamily.name: nav family
$navFamily.grade: same-answer (s251-D4 ladder). The three surfaces answer the same question — where am I and where can I go — in different shapes for different viewports. They are NOT drop-in and NOT same-shape: a masthead cannot be pasted where a rail was.
$navFamily.sharedAnatomy: .nv-item (icon / label / count / chevron), .nv-ic, .nv-label, .nv-count, .nv-chev — one class grammar, one meaning, in all three snippets. Hover, :active, :focus-visible, [aria-current=page] and [aria-disabled=true] are declared once in a SHARED ITEM block that is byte-identical in all three files.
$navFamily.sharedTokens: One NAV FAMILY TOKEN SET block: --nav-page --nav-surface --nav-text --nav-muted --nav-icon --nav-rule --nav-sub-rule --nav-hover --nav-pressed --nav-indicator --nav-focus --nav-disabled --nav-count-bg --nav-count-fg --nav-shadow --nav-scrim --nav-radius, plus the geometry vars --nav-w (248px) --nav-w-rail (64px) --nav-h (64px) --nav-row (44px). The block is byte-identical in Sidebar-nav and Tab-bar; Navigations carries it plus EXACTLY TWO extra vars (--field-border, --field-active) for the search field it alone contains. That is checkable by diff — the family claim is mechanical, not rhetorical.
$navFamily.indicatorRule: The 3px current-location bar sits on the EDGE THE NAV TOUCHES THE CONTENT. Sidebar: inline-start. Masthead: block-end. Tab bar: block-start. Masthead compact drawer: inline-start, because a stacked panel hangs beside its content. The RULE is what the three share, not the pixel.
$navFamily.currentLocationCarriers: Three, and colour is always last. (1) aria-current='page'. (2) A SHAPE: the 3px indicator bar's presence or absence — and in Tab-bar the filled (-active) glyph swap as well. (3) A surface change to tertiary/background/hover in Sidebar-nav and Navigations; Tab-bar SUBSTITUTES the glyph swap for the surface change, because a full-width fill on a 56px bottom row reads as a pressed button rather than as a place. MEASURED at #261 (notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-probe.json, 24 driven probes): the current tab-bar row computes background rgba(0,0,0,0) in all four themes, both modes — the substitution is a fact in the file, not an intention. Dave is astigmatic and red is a problem hue, so the bar is never asked to work alone.
openItems: SUPERCHARGE DARK. primary/border/default (#DB0011) on tertiary/background/hover measures 4.58 light / 3.01 dark in mono, legacy and console, and 3.89 light / 2.73 dark in Supercharge — a FAIL. It is not declared as a contrastPair because declaring it would be a green that cannot fail in the theme where it is false. Supercharge dark either needs its own current-location value or the pattern needs a non-red mark in that theme. Dave's.

TAB-BAR VOCABULARY. The #261 lane brief described Tab-bar as in-page section tabs; the gated Tabs component already is that, and Tab-bar's own meta has always said app-level BOTTOM navigation. Built to the canon meaning. The section-tab reading, drawn on these same tokens, is a PROPOSAL against Tabs in notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-review.html. Dave's.
$navFamily.drivenReceipt: notes/_lanes/261-N-drive-nav.py — 3 components x 4 themes x 2 modes = 24 driven probes, written to notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-probe.json and 24 PNGs. It measures, per theme: the indicator's computed box-shadow geometry against the family edge rule (0 mismatches in 24), the smallest visible .nv-item box (sidebar 247x44, masthead 218x44, tab bar 81x46 — all at or over the 44px control target), the count chip (24px on a row, 18px on a glyph — at or over the 24px dial-down floor), the disabled row's aria-disabled/tabindex pair, and the live contrast of primary/border/default on tertiary/background/hover. That last one reproduced the quoted four-theme figures exactly: 4.58 light / 3.01 dark in mono, legacy and console; 3.89 / 2.73 in SUPERCHARGE. The Supercharge failure is now a measurement, not a memory.
